metadata.source: U.S. Census Bureau ACS 5-Year Data Profiles & Passaic County 2026 Certified Rolls

zipCodeComparison.neighborhoodsIncluded: North Hawthorne & Goffle Brook Section, Central Hawthorne & Lincoln Ave Corridor
keyFindings: Certified composite property tax rate is 3.144%, with an equalization ratio of 73.91%.
Public education represents 54.2% of property taxes, while municipal operations account for 29.6%.
Average residential assessment is $380,637, producing an average annual tax bill of $11,967.23.

neighborhoods.name: North Hawthorne & Goffle Brook Section
neighborhoods.character: Picturesque suburban streets bordering Goffle Brook Park with stately colonials, cape cods, and deep landscaped lots
neighborhoods.description: Sought-after northern residential section bordering Ridgewood and Wyckoff, featuring charming parks and sports fields.
neighborhoods.taxDynamic: Stable residential assessment base with strong market resale values.

neighborhoods.name: Central Hawthorne & Lincoln Ave Corridor
neighborhoods.character: Walkable town center surrounding Lincoln Avenue and Diamond Bridge retail, featuring two-family homes and commuter rail station
neighborhoods.description: Community core centered around Hawthorne NJ Transit rail station and local dining along Lafayette and Lincoln avenues.
neighborhoods.taxDynamic: Mixed residential and light industrial ratables supporting municipal appropriations.

equityAnalysis.summary: Hawthorne Borough maintains a certified residential tax roll across its neighborhoods.

keyTakeaways.title: Property Tax Burden & Household Income
keyTakeaways.detail: In Hawthorne Borough, homeowners pay an average of $11,967.23 annually in property taxes, consuming approximately 10.3% of median household income.

keyTakeaways.title: Equalization Ratio & Revaluation Balance
keyTakeaways.detail: With an equalization ratio of 73.91%, assessed values average ~73.91% of current true market values, establishing the basis for certified county tax equalization.

keyTakeaways.title: School District vs Municipal Levy Split
keyTakeaways.detail: Local education represents 54.2% of the total tax bill, municipal government absorbs 29.6%, and Passaic County claims 16.2%.
